name: autofeature
description: Build an entire feature end-to-end from a single prompt. Pipeline: interrogate → scope → product-review → plan → branch → implement (parallel specialists) → test → review → ship → test-manifest. Review lenses unified under /review [product|feature|market|scope]: /product-review (CEO/PM/flow-walker whole-product gaps & flows), /feature-review (focused opinion + build advice for one feature), /market-review (market demand, competitive gap & VC fundability with cited, re-verified research), /scope. Also /test (acceptance-test the live app — web/iOS/Android — by driving it like a user, building its own test plan from what was built), /fullrun (deploy verification), /seo (SEO audit + fix), /copy (de-AI copy audit + rewrite + write, with per-project voice file) and /patterns (coding-pattern census → per-repo canon at .autofeature/patterns.md → establish + enforce + diff-check; the pipeline reads the canon in every run so specialists stop replicating drifted majorities). Backend shape: /backend-api-skills gets any backend API into the correct shape — audit it against the route → controller → service → model standard (a V1-V14 violation catalogue ranked by risk, not by clause order), create it right from the first commit (greenfield skeleton or one correctly-shaped domain slice), or fix drift with a behavior-preserving refactor gated on identical-green (a pre-existing route test that had to be edited means behavior changed, so revert). Stack-adaptive: it detects the repo's framework, ORM, validator and test runner and maps the four layers onto them rather than assuming Express+Mongoose, so the same standard applies to every backend you own. /api-standards is now a thin alias forwarding there with the Ritchies profile. Ritchies platform: /ritchies (cross-repo API+web+iOS+Android feature builder, API-first + pick-clients), backed by a kotlin-compose-architect specialist. iOS is deliberately NOT merged to main on ship — that merge ships a TestFlight build via .github/workflows/ios-release.yml on push to main — which runs NO tests, so a merge releases whatever is on main ungated; it is a release decision the user makes, not a tidy-up step. /ritchies-ios-test covers the iOS verification hand-off from a machine with no Xcode: pick the Mac session BY MACHINE NAME never by project name, demand the compile result before anything else, drive the simulator through simctl (device) + XCUITest (UI) and NEVER by controlling the screen — pixel-clicking fails silently when it lands on the wrong element, so a mis-driven pass is indistinguishable from a real one; screenshots are evidence, never the control mechanism, and an unaddressable element means adding an accessibility identifier rather than reaching for the pointer — and finish on one of four honest verdicts (built+simulator-verified / built+tests-green / compile-checked-only / never-compiled) with no warming one into another. Award interpretation: /award-map maps an Australian modern award into rosterio-compliance-service enumeration-first — transcribe the clause list and sub-clause counts from the Commission's PDF, triage every clause against the closed rule vocabulary, then author SQL against a fixed work list that only shrinks, so gap discovery terminates instead of looping. A merged PR isn't live — Step 9.5 gates promotion to the one deployed database (no staging tier exists) behind a re-run of verify/award-verify/closure against it and explicit sign-off. /award-verify closes the gap closure can't: independent re-derivation of every rule row from its clause text alone, diffed against what shipped, with an adversarial pass only where readers disagree — coverage proves a clause was read, this checks it was read correctly. /award-scenarios prices whole, real employment situations and has independent reasoners derive the expected pay from the award's own words, blind to what the engine produced — catching rule INTERACTIONS and silently-missing penalties that a per-row check cannot see. /award-ui generates test cases from the award's own thresholds, seeds a tenant for any mapped award from its declared employee-facts, and drives the manager screen in a browser to check the roster SHOWS what the engine decided. /award-drift is the manual, on-demand answer to whether the award's own wording moved since it was mapped — re-fetches the text, diffs clause-by-clause, flags when the pay database itself may need a fresh workbook, and re-authors with history preserved (closes the superseded row's operative_to rather than deleting it, since the engine already resolves shifts against operative_from/operative_to and a blind delete would silently break historical pricing). Model-tiered for cost — the fan-out runs on Sonnet/Haiku, Opus only for the few highest-judgment steps (tune in orchestrator/model-tiers.md). Browser testing no longer depends on typing a password: Claude in Chrome refuses password fields by design, so adapted/browser-session.md replaces the login step everywhere with a six-rung ladder (seeder emits sessions → dev-only 404-guarded /__test/login → same-origin fetch login so an httpOnly Set-Cookie lands in the real browser jar → token injected at the frontend's actual storage key → storage-state replay → the human's own session), detection that reads the repo's storage key, cookie flags and seeder instead of guessing, and a two-signal gate that refuses to walk a single flow until the API names the intended user AND the DOM shows a marker that cannot render anonymously — a session that silently did not take makes every flow fail for the same wrong reason and reads as a catastrophically broken product. Guarded on both ends: non-production targets and fixture credentials only, with a real person's password always rung 5 (they log in themselves). /ui-test is the browser-only driver built on it for apps that seed their own dummy data — seeds the fixtures, mints a session per role, walks each role's flows as that role, and keeps one deliberately-BLOCKED flow on the real login screen so "login is never tested" cannot hide inside a green run. /test and /award-ui share the same ladder.
